title: EOS provider adapters (opt-in)
description: Which external authorities this project lets EOS consult, and about what. Absent by default: with no providers, every gate still reaches a verdict offline. A provider can only ever raise a verdict EOS already reached on its own — an unavailable, unauthorised or broken provider leaves that verdict untouched, so adding one can never make a project worse off (ADR-005 D4).

adapter.description: `github-governance` verifies branch protection; `github-attestation` verifies artifact provenance; `mock` is deterministic and offline, for tests.

subjects.description: What this provider is authoritative about. `enforcement-authority` answers 'does the server enforce the gates'; `evidence-provenance' answers 'did this artifact come from the build it claims'.

options.description: Adapter-specific settings. A credential is never one of them: adapters delegate authentication to an already-authenticated CLI, so no token is read, stored or logged (ADR-005 D3).

throw.description: mock only — simulates an adapter that crashes
